sources.title: Introducing the AI Productivity Index for Accounting — official Mercor methodology article

access.note: The article is public. It says the open sample is one world and ten tasks; the held-out benchmark remains private and this record grants no redistribution rights.

observations.interpretation: Mercor's official July 31 article says the benchmark comprises 160 tasks across ten simulated companies. This is the paper/blog cohort, distinct from the current live leaderboard's displayed 100-task cohort.
The article describes ten simulated companies/worlds.
More than 40 accounting professionals authored and solved benchmark tasks.
The article reports median professional experience of 11 years.
More than half of the professionals had worked at a Big Four firm.
The article reports an average of 13.7 criteria per task.
The article reports 97% agreement between the open-source AI judge and expert graders; this is publisher-reported validation, not independent Mycelix validation.
A public sample set contains one world; the full held-out evaluation set remains private.
The open sample contains ten tasks and must not be confused with the private 160-task paper cohort or live 100-task page.
The article says agent responses when clarification is needed are outside benchmark scope.

observations.display_locator: Why do models fail, article line 65
observations.interpretation: For the top three models, roughly seven in ten failures were attributed to flawed reasoning rather than inability to retrieve information. A described failure is a discrepancy identified mid-workflow but omitted or contradicted in the final journal.

observations.display_locator: What the leaderboard measures, article line 60
observations.interpretation: The article reports the purpose-built Ramp Harness improves Mean Criteria@3 by 1.2 points on average relative to Loop Harness; it explicitly says this does not evaluate the complete Ramp Stack product.

observations.display_locator: What the leaderboard measures, article line 61
observations.interpretation: The Ramp Harness ablation is not an evaluation of the full Stack product's integrations, memory, controls, auditability or spreadsheet tooling.

sources.notes: This publisher article provides methodology detail absent from the leaderboard summary: 160-task original held-out cohort, >40 expert authors, median 11 years experience, 13.7 mean rubric criteria/task, 97% judge/expert agreement and a one-world/ten-task public sample. It also explains that the canonical leaderboard uses Loop Harness, while a purpose-built Ramp Harness is a separate ablation and not a test of the full Ramp Stack.

observations.interpretation: Gemini 4 Argon High is the highest displayed configuration at 71.5% ±4.8. This aggregate is not directly comparable with the 160-task paper's 56.4% Mean Criteria@3.

The results section indicates 46 model configurations are available in the full results view; the top-five list is not the full ranking.
The live leaderboard states its canonical Mean Criteria metric uses k=4, while the paper/blog report Mean Criteria@3. Preserve the attempt count in any reproduction.
Each model is run eight times for Pass@1, Pass@8 and Pass^8; do not assume this is the same attempt aggregation as Mean Criteria k=4.

observations.observed_value: step reruns until success; persistent failures up to three trajectory reruns
observations.interpretation: The live methodology says step-level response issues are rerun until success; persistent system errors or model failures can cause up to three trajectory reruns. A faithful matched reproduction must report infra retries separately from capability failures and disclose whether this exact policy is applied.
Leaderboard uses a five-million-token cap per run.
Leaderboard uses a 500-step cap per run.
The page says confidence intervals are 95% task-level bootstraps over 10,000 resamples.
The 100-task cohort averages 7.5 required input files per task.

observations.observed_value: task prompt, criterion and model final answer
observations.interpretation: The language-model judge grades each rubric criterion independently as met/not met, sees the task prompt, criterion and final model answer, and penalizes scattergunning. It does not inspect an independently recorded agent evidence trace unless that trace is submitted in the final answer.

observations.observed_value: highest available reasoning setting unless stated otherwise
observations.interpretation: Unless otherwise stated, models run at their highest available reasoning setting. This setting is part of benchmark run provenance.
